title: FireRunner
description: Ephemeral Firecracker microVMs for GitLab CI (github.com/ismoilovdevml/firerunner)

list.name: node
list.label: Node exporter
list.description: node_exporter of the same hosts: relabel both jobs' instance to the host name.

panels.title: Daemon loop age
panels.description: Seconds since the daemon's main loop last completed a pass (it passes every 2 s), as of the last scrape: normally no more than the scrape interval. Over 120 s /healthz fails and FireRunnerDaemonUnhealthy fires. No data: the daemon is not scraped.

panels.title: Flintlock API
panels.description: Whether the daemon's last flintlock listing answered. Down: no microVM can be created and new jobs fail in prepare (FireRunnerFlintlockDown after 3 min).

panels.title: FireRunner failure rate (24h)
panels.description: Share of jobs that failed because of FireRunner or the host (system failures, not cancelled). Failing project scripts are not counted.

panels.title: Job slots in use
panels.description: Running jobs / gitlab-runner concurrent. At 100 % new jobs wait in GitLab until one finishes; the counts are in Jobs > Running jobs, ready pool VMs and concurrent.

panels.title: Cold boots (1h)
panels.description: Share of jobs in the last hour that found no ready pool VM and booted their own. Above ~20 %: raise pool.size, if memory allows.

panels.title: Host resources used
panels.description: The fullest host for each resource jobs wait for or fail on when it runs out. Thin pool: microVM disks (alerts at 85 % data, 75 % metadata). Memory committed: guest memory promised to microVMs against the admission limit; at 100 % new microVMs wait. DHCP leases: at 100 % new microVMs get no address (alert at 80 %). Disk: saved builder caches and flintlock's microVM state (alert at 85 %). A missing bar: the value is unknown (thin pool: lvs fails).

panels.title: Pool ready
panels.description: Pre-booted microVMs waiting for a job.

panels.title: microVMs
panels.description: All microVMs flintlock knows, in any state: pool, job and builder VMs and `firerunner run` VMs.

panels.title: Jobs (24h)
panels.description: Jobs finished in the last 24 h, any result: the volume behind the failure rate.

panels.title: Prepare p50 (pool)
panels.description: Median time a job waited for its microVM when a pool VM was ready, over the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Prepare p50 (cold)
panels.description: Median time a job waited for its microVM when it had to boot one, over the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Warm builds
panels.description: Share of jobs running docker build that got their project's builder warm (ready) over the last 24 h. The rest waited for it to boot and restore its cache, or built without it. Low: raise builder.max or keep builders longer (builder.idle_ttl).

panels.title: Builder boot
panels.description: Median time from creating a builder to it answering, over 24 h: VM boot plus the restore of its saved layer cache. A build that finds its builder booting waits for this.

panels.title: Job p50
panels.description: Median job duration, prepare to cleanup, over the last 24 h.

panels.title: Job p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of job duration over the last 24 h.

panels.title: CPU steal
panels.description: Share of CPU time the hypervisor gave to other VMs while this host wanted it, over 1 h (node_exporter). Only on a host that is itself a VM; above a few percent jobs run slower than the CPU count suggests.

panels.title: Running jobs, ready pool VMs and concurrent
panels.description: Jobs in progress against gitlab-runner's concurrent limit, and the pre-booted VMs waiting for the next job. Running at concurrent: new jobs wait in GitLab. Ready pool VMs at 0 while jobs start: they cold-boot.

panels.title: Jobs finished per minute
panels.description: Finished jobs by result: success, script_failure (the job's own commands) and system_failure (FireRunner or the host, cancelled and timed-out jobs included).

panels.title: Job start latency (prepare), p50 / p95
panels.description: Time from job start to a ready microVM. 'pool' = claimed a pre-booted VM, 'cold' = booted one.

panels.title: Cold-boot share
panels.description: Share of prepared jobs that found no ready pool VM and booted their own. High while jobs run: pool.size is too small, or host memory keeps the pool from refilling.

panels.title: Jobs that waited over 30 s for memory
panels.description: Jobs that waited more than 30 s for host memory before their microVM was created; only jobs that found no ready pool VM wait. FireRunnerJobsWaitForMemory fires on 3 in 30 min, if they are over 10 % of the jobs.

panels.title: System failures by reason
panels.description: Jobs FireRunner or the host failed, by reason. Cancelled and timed-out jobs (reason canceled) are left out, as in the failure rate. See Operations > Alerts > FireRunnerSystemFailures.

panels.title: Job duration p50 / p95
panels.description: How long jobs take from prepare to cleanup.

panels.title: Seconds per job by stage
panels.description: Where a job's time goes: the average seconds a job spends in each gitlab-runner stage (script: the job's own steps). Compare with the old runners stage by stage: get_sources, restore_cache and the uploads are FireRunner's cost around the job's own work.

panels.title: Stage duration p95 by stage
panels.description: 95th percentile of each gitlab-runner stage. script: the job's own commands, docker build included; get_sources: the git clone; restore_cache / archive_cache: the cache: store. A stage that grows alone points at its cause.

panels.title: Pool
panels.description: Pre-booted microVMs ready for a job and booting, against pool.size (target).

panels.title: microVMs by state
panels.description: Every microVM flintlock knows (pool, job, builder, run) by its flintlock state.

panels.title: microVM boot time p95
panels.description: Time from create request to SSH ready, by kind: pool, cold (a job's own boot) and builder (includes waiting for memory and loading the saved cache).

panels.title: Boot failures and reconciled VMs
panels.description: microVMs that did not become ready, by kind (pool_dead: a pool VM dead when claimed), and microVMs reconcile deleted, by reason (see Reference > Metrics).

panels.title: Docker builds by builder per minute
panels.description: Jobs that ran docker build, by what their project's builder was when they got it. ready: warm layer cache. booting: the builder was starting (its cache is restored if one was saved). busy: all builder slots were in use, the job built without the cache. none: no builder (the daemon did not answer). Many busy: raise builder.max or lower builder.memory_mb.

panels.title: Builders by state and slots
panels.description: Builder microVMs, ready and booting, against builder.max (slots; 0 while builders are disabled). With every slot taken, a project without a builder only gets one by evicting a builder idle for 10 min; otherwise its jobs build without the cache.

panels.title: Builder removals by reason
panels.description: Why builders went away. lru (its slot was needed), idle, max_age and config_changed keep their cache for the project's next builder; not_answering and vm_gone are builders that died (FireRunnerBuildersFailing); operator: builder rm; disabled: builders turned off. Frequent lru: builder.max is too small for the projects that build.

panels.title: Builder cache copies by result
panels.description: Layer caches copied to the host when a builder is removed (save), loaded into the project's next builder (restore), and saved caches deleted to make room (evict). save skipped: larger than builder.saved_cache_gb, no room on the disk, or removed by builder rm meanwhile. restore missing: nothing saved; stale: saved by another builder image, dropped. failed: journalctl -u firerunner | grep 'builder cache'.

panels.title: Builds on a warm builder
panels.description: Share of jobs running docker build that got a warm builder, over the past hour at each point. Each drop is builds that waited for a booting builder or built without the cache.

panels.title: Builder ready time p50 / p95
panels.description: Time from creating a builder to it answering: VM boot plus the restore of its saved layer cache (about 100 MB/s on the trial host). Large caches restore slowly; builder.cache_mb caps them.

panels.title: Builder boot by phase
panels.description: Where builders spend their boot over the selected time range, slowest share first. admit: waiting for host memory; vm: create until SSH answers; save_wait: waiting for the project's previous builder to copy its cache out; restore: loading the saved cache (about 90 MB/s, so it grows with the cache); buildkitd: start until jobs can reach it. Share: the phase's seconds over all builder boot seconds, failed boots included. Boots: how many boots reached the phase; p50 and p90 of a few boots say little. One boot in detail: journalctl -u firerunner | grep 'builder boot phases'.

panels.title: Thin pool usage
panels.description: devmapper thin pool usage, read with lvs every 15 s. Alerts at 85 % data and 75 % metadata; a gap: lvs failed (FireRunnerThinPoolUnknown).

panels.title: Host memory available
panels.description: MemAvailable on the host. Guest memory is taken lazily, so this falls as microVMs use theirs; near 0 the kernel OOM-kills (FireRunnerHostOOMKill).

panels.title: Committed microVM memory by role
panels.description: What admission counts, by role; the capacity line is where new VMs start to wait. A growing job share with few running jobs means leaked VMs.

panels.title: DHCP leases
panels.description: Leased microVM addresses. At capacity jobs get no lease; a growing stale share means leases of deleted VMs are not released.

panels.title: Disk free
panels.description: Free space on the file systems of the saved builder caches (/var/lib/firerunner/builder-cache) and flintlock's microVM state (/var/lib/flintlock/vm); the fullest host per directory. Below 10 % of the file system no builder cache is saved; FireRunnerDiskFilling fires under 15 %.

panels.title: Flintlock errors per minute
panels.description: Failed flintlock calls of the daemon by RPC and gRPC code; every failed try of a retried listing counts. Unavailable: flintlockd is down or restarting; DeadlineExceeded: no answer in time.

panels.title: Daemon loop age and host OOM kills
panels.description: Seconds since the daemon main loop last passed (normally no more than the scrape interval) and processes the host kernel OOM-killed.

panels.title: Services
panels.description: systemd services the daemon checks every 15 s, and the flintlock API.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the host booted.

panels.title: CPUs
panels.description: CPU threads of the host.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Total memory of the host.

panels.title: Load 5m per CPU
panels.description: 5-minute load average per CPU thread. Above 1: runnable tasks wait for a CPU.

panels.title: IO wait
panels.description: Share of CPU time spent waiting for disk, over the last hour. High: the disk under the thin pool and the caches is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Swap in use. microVM memory that swaps makes every job on the host slow.

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Share of all CPU threads by mode. user/system: jobs and Firecracker; iowait: waiting for disk; steal: the hypervisor running other VMs (nested virtualization shows here).

panels.title: Pressure stall (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time some tasks waited for CPU, memory or IO. The earliest sign that the host is saturated and jobs slow down, before utilization reaches 100 %.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Host memory. microVMs keep the memory their guests touched, so used memory grows with builders and stays; available is what new microVMs can still get.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes read and written per second by disk. Builder cache copies and image pulls show here.

panels.title: Disk latency per operation
panels.description: Average time per read and write by disk. Tens of milliseconds while jobs run: the storage under the host is slow or shared.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time each disk had IO in flight. Near 100 %: the disk is the limit.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Bytes per second by interface: the uplink (NAT, registry pushes, git) and the microVM bridge.

panels.title: File systems used
panels.description: Share used of each mounted file system (the thin pool is in the Host row above).
